gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans reads wide and generous, its tall lowercase and sweeping s curves giving every line room to breathe. Fira Sans holds that openness paragraph after paragraph, while Neuropol's slim, closed futuristic letters stay up top.
gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-nunito: Neuropol draws a flat, unswelling line around every curve, which gives it a digital hum. Nunito follows with big round bowls and terminals that finish clear of the stem, so a long passage feels soft and approachable.
gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Futuristic and tightly closed, Neuropol sets a digital tone at the top. But Pilcrow Rounded answers with a tall lowercase, big counters and curves that refuse to close, a warm, open counterweight.
gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-public-sans: Neuropol's slim channel where the c opens gives its closed, single-weight letters a distinctly futuristic, digital look. Public Sans adds hefty, open trustworthy text beneath.
gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-quicksand: Quicksand reads soft, with tall bowls like blown glass bulbs. Its open, light-handed curves meet Neuropol's closed, futuristic letters, and that clash of tight against open is what defines the pair.
gen-dafont-neuropol-general-sans: General Sans fills the line with a tall x-height and smooth, unobstructed bends. General Sans is the open, steady half here, and Neuropol's closed digital letters make it look all the more relaxed.
gen-dafont-neuropol-nunito-sans: Soft and neutral, Nunito Sans opens its small letters wide beneath a Neuropol heading. Neuropol does its best work as a gentle, single-weight futuristic line, but Nunito Sans does its best in open-mouthed curves that carry the reading.
gen-dafont-neuropol-switzer: Switzer reads tubular and wire-like, with a tall waist line. If Neuropol were made small, its closed, futuristic letters would lose their slim channel, while Switzer holds up in a more approachable Swiss way.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-fs-amulya: Pulled-apart letters, glowing like neon. Neuropolitical's single stroke width runs through the whole alphabet, and Amulya's generous curve gaps give it a contemporary, modern partner underneath.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-fs-chillax: Chillax reads casual and relaxed, its line like spaghetti laid out in letters, with pen-lifted curves leaving loops unfinished. Neuropolitical's neon tubes are the tidy foil.
